title: Musculus: believe about God, believe God, believe in God
source_text: XXVIII. Musculus similiter fidei tres gradus sive partes assignat. Sed illas aliter explicat. Prima pars fidei ipsi est qua quaedam de Deo credimus: Veluti, quod sit Deus, quod sit unicus, omnipotens coeli & terrae creator, &c. Quod Christus sit Dei filius unigenitus, verus Deus, & verus homo, Redemptor & Mediator noster, &c. Et quod Spiritus Sanctus sit divinitate Patri & Filio aequalis, mentium illuminator, paracletus, doctor, consolator, &c. Secunda fidei pars est qua credimus Deo, hoc est, verbo ejus fidem adhibemus, tanquam Dei Verbo, de cujus veritate prorsus infallibili impium sit dubitare. Tertia fidei pars est qua credimus in Deum. Credere autem in Deum dicit esse spem omnem in Deum dirigere, firmaque fiducia ab illius bonitate pendere. In locis communibus Sacrae Theologiae, loco communi de Fide.
pass_a_gloss: Musculus similarly assigns three degrees or parts of faith. But he explains them otherwise. The first part of faith for him is that by which we believe certain things concerning God: for example, that God is, that He is one, almighty creator of heaven and earth, &c. That Christ is the only-begotten Son of God, true God and true man, our Redeemer and Mediator, &c. And that the Holy Spirit is equal in divinity to the Father and the Son, illuminator of minds, advocate, teacher, comforter, &c. The second part of faith is that by which we believe God, that is, we give credit to His word as the Word of God, of whose wholly infallible truth it would be impious to doubt. The third part of faith is that by which we believe in God. But to believe in God he says is to direct all hope to God, and to depend with firm trust upon His goodness. In the Common Places of Sacred Theology, the common place on Faith.
pass_b_english: 1. Believe certain things about God, Christ, and the Spirit.
2. Believe God — credit His word as infallible Word of God.
3. Believe in God — direct all hope to Him; depend with firm trust on His goodness.
